es: Redactar el calendario de un proyecto con plazos (future perfect), acciones en curso (future continuous) y tareas delegadas (have/get something done).

teaching.en: By the end of March, we will have signed the lease, and meanwhile Sara will be comparing quotes for the shelves.
teaching.es: Para finales de marzo habremos firmado el contrato de alquiler y, mientras tanto, Sara estará comparando presupuestos para las estanterías.
teaching.explanationEs: By + will have + participio marca lo terminado antes del plazo; will be + -ing, lo que está en curso.
segments: By the end of March, we will have signed the lease,
and meanwhile Sara will be comparing quotes for the shelves.
teaching.audioText: By the end of March, we will have signed the lease, and meanwhile Sara will be comparing quotes for the shelves.

teaching.en: The first milestone is to open by the first of June, a hard deadline on which everything else in the timeline depends.
teaching.es: El primer hito es abrir para el uno de junio, un plazo improrrogable del que depende todo lo demás en el calendario.
teaching.explanationEs: Milestone es un hito importante; a hard deadline no admite prórroga.
segments: The first milestone is to open by the first of June,
a hard deadline on which everything else in the timeline depends.
teaching.audioText: The first milestone is to open by the first of June, a hard deadline on which everything else in the timeline depends.

teaching.en: If the permit is delayed, the whole project could fall behind schedule, so Leo will push back the opening rather than cut corners.
teaching.es: Si se retrasa el permiso, todo el proyecto podría quedar con retraso, así que Leo aplazará la apertura en lugar de hacer las cosas a medias.
teaching.explanationEs: Push back = aplazar; behind schedule = con retraso respecto al calendario.
segments: If the permit is delayed, the whole project could fall behind schedule,
so Leo will push back the opening rather than cut corners.
teaching.audioText: If the permit is delayed, the whole project could fall behind schedule, so Leo will push back the opening rather than cut corners.

teaching.en: Leo will delegate the accounts to Sara, and he will sign off on each invoice only after she has checked it.
teaching.es: Leo delegará la contabilidad en Sara y dará el visto bueno a cada factura solo después de que ella la haya revisado.
teaching.explanationEs: Delegate + tarea + to + persona; sign off on = dar el visto bueno de forma definitiva.
segments: Leo will delegate the accounts to Sara, and he will sign
off on each invoice only after she has checked it.
teaching.audioText: Leo will delegate the accounts to Sara, and he will sign off on each invoice only after she has checked it.

teaching.en: We are getting the permit approved by the council this week, and Leo is having the sign made by a carpenter.
teaching.es: Esta semana estamos gestionando que el municipio apruebe el permiso, y Leo está encargando el cartel a un carpintero.
teaching.explanationEs: Have/get + objeto + participio expresa que otra persona hace la tarea: the permit approved, the sign made.
segments: We are getting the permit approved by the council this week,
and Leo is having the sign made by a carpenter.
teaching.audioText: We are getting the permit approved by the council this week, and Leo is having the sign made by a carpenter.

teaching.en: If every task can stay on track, the timeline holds; this time next month, we will be painting the walls.
teaching.es: Si cada tarea puede mantenerse según lo previsto, el calendario se mantiene; dentro de un mes estaremos pintando las paredes.
teaching.explanationEs: Stay on track = mantenerse según lo previsto; this time next month + will be + -ing describe una acción en curso.
segments: If every task can stay on track, the timeline holds;
this time next month, we will be painting the walls.
teaching.audioText: If every task can stay on track, the timeline holds; this time next month, we will be painting the walls.

feedback.es: El futuro perfecto es will have + participio: indica una tarea terminada antes del plazo.

origin.text: The shop must be ready before the doors open. By the fifteenth of May, the carpenter will ___ finished the shelves.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase describe correctamente lo que hace Leo?

Leo is having a carpenter to build the sign and a painter paint the walls painted.
Leo is having built the sign by a carpenter and painted the walls by a painter.

feedback.es: La estructura es have + objeto + participio (the sign built, the walls painted) + by + quien lo hace.

origin.text: Leo does not make things himself. He pays a carpenter to build the sign and a painter to paint the walls.

Ask the suppliers to delay their deliveries until the permit arrives.

feedback.es: Leo prefiere aplazar la apertura una semana antes que abrir sin el permiso.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estas frases expresa el segundo calendario?

From Friday at noon, the painters finish everything.
By Friday at noon, the painters will have finished everything.

feedback.es: By + will have + participio marca un plazo: todo terminado antes del mediodía; will be finishing describiría una acción en curso.

origin.text: The owners are comparing two schedules for the week before the opening. In the first, the painters work all Friday; in the second, they must have everything finished by Friday at noon.

prompt.es: Redacta el calendario de apertura: dos futuros, dos encargos y un plazo.

answer.text: Here is the timeline for opening the workshop. By the end of March, we will have signed the lease, and meanwhile Leo is having the sign made by a carpenter. We are also getting the permit approved by the council, which should be ready by the fifteenth of April; if it is delayed, we will push back the opening rather than open without it. In the middle of May, we will be putting up the shelves and painting the walls, while Sara will be building the website. Leo will delegate the accounts to Sara, so that he can concentrate on the tools and the first customers. By the first of June, we will have opened the doors, which is our hard deadline. The first milestone is to repair fifty bikes in the first month, and we will review the plan together in July to check that we are still on track.

Leo will delegate the accounts to Sara, so that he can look after the tools and the first customers. By the first of June, we will have opened the workshop, which is a hard deadline. Our plan for the opening is as follows. By the middle of April, we will have received the lease papers, and Leo is having the sign built by a carpenter. Meanwhile, we are getting the permit approved by the council, and by the end of May we will have painted the walls. In June we will be welcoming our first customers, and Sara will be running the website. Leo will delegate the accounts to Sara, which leaves him free to work on the tools. Our first milestone is fifty repairs in the first month, and we will stay on track by reviewing the plan together every week. By the first of June, we will have opened the doors, and that is a hard deadline for everyone.

feedback.es: Un buen calendario combina plazos con will have, acciones en curso con will be + -ing, encargos con have/get y una tarea delegada.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada estructura con lo que expresa en un calendario.

feedback.es: Cada estructura cumple una función: plazo cumplido, acción en curso, tarea delegada y aplazamiento.
